edges.rationale: Understanding what an agent is and how it perceives and acts is required before learning the specific external capabilities (tools) it uses to act.
The core definition of autonomous action and decision-making is the foundation for learning how agents decompose tasks and sequence actions.
Planning how to solve complex problems requires knowing what tools are available to direct toward goal completion.
Tool misuse is a specific agentic failure mode, so understanding tools is needed to understand how they can be misused.
Error propagation in multi-step reasoning and infinite loops arise from the planning and action-sequencing layer, so planning must be understood first.
